journal_lines: §oWet stone and old water — the smell of a cave that had been working on itself for a long time. Good ore smell underneath.
§aStalactites the height of small trees. §lWoodcutter§a set the props. Miner reached the walls. Neither alone would have managed.
Ceiling looked wrong. Braced it with fresh-cut timber before touching the rock face. Good call.
§aThe dripstone had cracked the good ore open over years. We took advantage. Props held the whole time.
Axe cut the supports. Pickaxe worked the seam. The cave dripped on both operations equally.
§oConstant drip kept time while the woodcutter and the miner traded turns. §aDeep work. Worth it.
Water on every surface. Brought timber down in sections, set them vertically in the wet floor. Did the work.
§aCame out damp. The ore came out dry, mostly. §lDripstone§a cavern pays if you prop it right.
